title: Jesus Demands This Heart of Mine
description: Jesus Demands This Heart of Mine in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 329 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Sense of Sin”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus de-mands this heart of mine, De-mands my love, my joy, my care, But ah, how dead to things di-vine, How cold my best af-fec-tions are!

lines: Jesus demands this heart of mine,
Demands my love, my joy, my care,
But ah, how dead to things divine,
How cold my best affections are!
Divides my Saviour from my sight;
O, for one happy, shining hour
Come, gracious Lord; thy love can raise
My captive powers from sin and death,
And fill my heart and life with praise,
And tune my last, expiring breath.

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
